biography: Laurents Hörr, born in Trier, Germany, in 1988, wasn't born into a racing dynasty, but rather stumbled into motorsport through a local karting track. His father, a baker, initially scoffed at the idea, but relented after Laurents badgered him relentlessly, showcasing surprising talent from his very first laps. Laurents quickly dominated the regional karting scene, his flashy, aggressive style earning him both fans and detractors. A defining moment came during a national karting championship, where, despite starting at the back due to a mechanical failure, he clawed his way to victory, overtaking the leader on the final corner with a daring move that became legendary in karting circles. That win secured him sponsorship and a path into single-seaters. While he never quite reached Formula 1, he carved out a successful career in sports car racing, becoming a stalwart of the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship. Now, at 36, he's considered to be at the peak of his powers, driving the #20 Oreca 07, aiming for overall victory at Daytona and beyond, a testament to his relentless pursuit of speed and glory. Despite the success, he never forgets his roots, often visiting the Trier karting track to mentor young aspiring racers, sharing the lessons he learned the hard way.
drivingStyle: Hörr's driving style can be described as flamboyant and aggressive. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to take risks in overtaking situations, often pushing the limits of grip and sometimes beyond. While this approach has occasionally led to costly mistakes, it has also delivered spectacular results. He has a knack for extracting maximum performance from the car, especially in qualifying, and is adept at managing tire wear despite his aggressive style, adapting his technique as the race progresses to maintain a competitive pace. He excels in wet conditions, where his car control and risk-taking ability give him a significant advantage.
